races.name: Coca-Cola HBC Ireland And Northern Ireland 3-Y-O Hurdle

runners_data.name: Nicky Larson
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner in the race with a win and a place on good ground over comparable distances; Sean Flanagan takes the ride for Paul Nolan whose yard has struck once from four in the last 14 days — going and trip pose no concern, and the uncontested lead is its most powerful asset, though the STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence if it cannot quite dominate as projected.
runners_data.comment: Nicky Larson arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip, giving him a solid profile at the head of the weights on 158 lb; 18 days between runs is plenty fresh enough to go again.

runners_data.name: Camp Verde
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's runner has had two runs on similar going but both resulted in finishes outside the frame, and the fade-in-finish flag is a genuine red light in a race that could become a sprint; Michael Kenneally rides on a tight eight-day turnaround, and Camp Verde will need to find more than its record suggests to justify prominence here.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Camp Verde has been yet to win in his last two starts — including an unseating — but returns quickly after just eight days and, lightly raced, there is plenty more to learn about him.

runners_data.name: Fay Og
runners_data.note: Crawford's hold-up performer has three runs on good ground without troubling the judge and arrives 102 days fresh; a true rear-of-field type by nature, it is mapped to midfield because the race holds more closers than positions allow — Slevin's experience gives it some hope of finding a gap, but the fade warning and poor recent form make it a tough each-way proposition.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Fay Og has had time to develop over 102 days away and carries 152 lb on his first start — connections will be hoping he can make an immediate impact.

runners_data.name: Nod Of Approval
runners_data.note: Harrington's yard is active and has placed two from 29 runners in the last fortnight; Nod Of Approval is a genuine hold-up horse whose best run was a second at 12f on good ground, and it returns wearing a tongue-tie — consistent record in similar conditions but has never won, and the uncontested pace scenario is not ideally suited.
runners_data.comment: Nod Of Approval catches the eye on his profile here, carrying 152 lb on a competitive mark and returning on a lively 18-day turnaround with our rating of 83 placing him third in the field; the risk is that he is yet to score in recent starts, that sole effort a seventh.

runners_data.name: Point Star
runners_data.note: Mark Fahey's entry is completely unexposed with an unknown running style and no going data to draw on; Thomas O'Connor claims 7lb, which softens the weight burden, but the absence of any trip or going evidence makes this a pure unknown — could surprise on debut but punters are flying blind entirely.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Point Star is a complete unknown but lightly raced profiles like his often leave room for significant improvement; carrying 152 lb on his first start, he is yet to score but there is plenty to learn about him here.

runners_data.name: Moon Aura
runners_data.note: McBratney's 3-y-o has five runs all on good or good-to-soft ground without winning, and Kevin Sexton takes the ride; it races prominently and will aim to sit just off Nicky Larson's heels, but six is the best it has managed in five hurdle starts and the flat form over shorter trips does not scream staying power at 2m1½f.
runners_data.comment: Unraced and therefore unexposed, Moon Aura steps into the unknown on debut after 59 days off the track, carrying 145 lb, with plenty of potential still to be uncovered.

runners_data.name: No Bother Aoife
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's yard is in strong form (7 from 30 in 14 days) and No Bother Aoife has the most consistent recent record in the field, placing four times from its last nine runs including a third at 16f on good ground; it is a genuine hold-up horse by nature, operating closer to the action in this map due to congestion at the rear — the position compromise is a real concern given its form requires a strong pace to deliver its best.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and fourth two starts back, No Bother Aoife arrives fit on an 18-day turnaround with distance experience to call on and a rating of 90 that marks her out as a leading threat; the risk is she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Sands Castle
runners_data.note: Adrian Sexton's runner carries the head-hood for the first time and arrives on the back of a single hurdles run (sixth at 16f) on the same going type; Harry Sexton claims 7lb, but the fade flag, modest form profile, and first-time headgear make this a speculative entry at best over a trip it has not conquered.
runners_data.comment: Sands Castle has been off for just 18 days and returns at a workable weight of 145 lb, with our rating of 79 marking her as a genuine player in this field; the main concern is that she heads here winless from her last start and must find improvement.

runners_data.name: Swift Charm
runners_data.note: Crawford's second runner in the race has had five hurdle starts without winning and the fade-in-finish flag appears repeatedly in its profile; it wears tongue-tie and hood, has some placed efforts over 10f on good ground, but the 55-day break and a form line that shows no serious threat to rivals of this grade make it difficult to strongly recommend.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Swift Charm steps into the spotlight here carrying 145 lb after a 55-day absence, yet to score but with plenty still to find out about her.

races.paceDynamic: Nicky Larson is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner 3-Y-O hurdle at Down Royal, and with no rival willing or able to seriously challenge for the lead, the early pace is likely to be sustainable rather than searingly fast on good-to-firm ground. Camp Verde and Moon Aura will push to be prominent behind the leader, creating a compressed early order where the front end of the race is not truly contested but is occupied. This moderate, uncontested tempo over 2m1½f on a sound surface suits horses who can travel fluently in the first three or four and produce a quality finish rather than those relying on a strong pace to deliver late energy. The field holds more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate: No Bother Aoife and Fay Og are true rear-of-field types who will likely find themselves pushed closer to midfield than their natural position, meaning their natural hold-up patterns are compromised and the advantage flows to genuine prominent racers who can dictate their own destiny from the front third. **The overall shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead profiles who can travel kindly through a modest gallop and kick when required.**

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Nicky Larson Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Nicky Larson bowls along in front unchallenged and converts a comfortable lead into a winning advantage on the run-in.
scenarios.body: Nicky Larson, though officially rated as prominent, has demonstrated a front-running capability across recent hurdles on good ground, and a lone uncontested lead on good-to-firm Down Royal should allow it to dictate a race run at a tempo entirely of its own choosing; the likely fade from rivals who cannot reproduce their natural positions boosts its prospects considerably. Prominent horses who travel sweetly and can sustain their rhythm into the straight are the prime beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Rival Gets Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If Camp Verde or Moon Aura travel comfortably just off Nicky Larson and produce a better finish when the pace eases in the straight.
scenarios.body: A modest gallop can set up a sprint finish from the top of the straight, and any prominent horse with residual finishing kick can overhaul a tiring leader who has done all the donkey work; Camp Verde's recent runs on similar going suggest it can track the pace, though its tendency to fade in the finish is a material concern. Moon Aura, consistent at this trip on good ground, is the cleaner candidate from this position if it finds more than its flat-racing figures suggest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to create an opportunity for one of the redistributed hold-up horses to finish with real purpose.
scenarios.body: No Bother Aoife or Nod Of Approval, both genuine hold-up types, would need either a stronger gallop than projected or a race that strings out enough to give them a clear passage; the structural problem is that No Bother Aoife is mapped into midfield out of role, limiting the clean late run it needs. Nod Of Approval has some track form on good ground and the Harrington yard is operating at a steady clip, which gives it the most credible late claim if the pace scenario shifts.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart; Chaos Wins
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses challenge for prominent positions early, the pace becomes uneven, and a more adaptable or well-handicapped runner capitalises on the resulting scramble.
scenarios.body: Should Camp Verde or Moon Aura push aggressively for position early and disturb Nicky Larson's rhythm, the race could become ragged and messy, opening the door for a horse like No Bother Aoife to creep into contention through the gaps. Point Star is a wildcard here given its unknown style and lightly-raced profile — it could prove adaptable if connections have it primed for this sharp test.

watchPoints.text: Nicky Larson could steal a march with a clean break and establish an unassailable lead — watch whether it hacks into the first two hurdles unchallenged, because if it does the race may effectively be over early.

Camp Verde's fade tendency is a red flag for connections backing it into the closing stages — monitor whether it can sustain its prominent position from the fourth-last hurdle onward or visibly ties up on the run-in.

No Bother Aoife's ability to get a clean passage is the key variable for late drama — if the midfield gets congested between the last two hurdles, Conor Stone-Walsh will need to be proactive or the hold-up run will arrive too late.

Point Star is a complete unknown in terms of running style and ability — watch the early exchanges to identify whether Thomas O'Connor settles it or sends it forward, as that will immediately clarify whether it is a shape-breaker or irrelevant.

Nod Of Approval's tongue-tie is new headgear worth monitoring — if the gear change unlocks extra comfort in the early stages and it settles better than usual, the Harrington runner has the profile to creep into contention from the rear on good-to-firm ground.

races.name: Dale Farm Dromona Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Cosmic Front
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins-trained five-year-old carrying top weight, prominent style suits a controlled pace scenario perfectly; 203 days off the track is worth monitoring but the booking of Brian Hayes for a Mullins mare in a maiden is a strong stable signal.

runners_data.name: Churchfield Annie
runners_data.note: Has placed four times from five starts on Good ground and clearly handles the going well; the tongue tie is fitted again and Emmet Mullins keeps her competitive after a 47-day break, making her a consistent threat from a handy position.

runners_data.name: Howaya Codge
runners_data.note: Showed a tendency to fade late on her only start and her hold-up style is her natural mode, though the deep field of closers means she is unlikely to find her preferred position at the rear; Simon Torrens will need to improvise from midfield.

runners_data.name: Jo's Secret
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up operator with two placed efforts on Good ground, including a second over 2m on similar terms; Kevin Sexton will likely settle her quietly and she represents the most credible late threat among the true closers if the pace does any sorting.

runners_data.name: Loughdoo
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, she will control matters from the front but has faded in her finishes and her trainer has had no runners in the last 14 days; the novice 7lb claimer Harry Sexton reduces her weight but the tendency to stop in the closing stages is a genuine concern.

runners_data.name: Messonghi
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and almost unknown — fell on her only start over 2m on Good ground; the unknown style rating adds further uncertainty and P J Rothwell's in-form yard (3 from 13 in 14 days) is the main reason to keep her in mind.

runners_data.name: Saoirses Choice
runners_data.note: Three career runs all result in single-figure finishes with no placed efforts; she fades in the finish and two recent ninths on Good ground suggest she will need a significant step forward to trouble the principals.

runners_data.name: Clanokre Lass
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old has been placed just once from three starts and her natural hold-up style places her at the back, though the crowded rear means she is mapped to midfield and will not get the patient ride that suits her best.

runners_data.name: Rare Times
runners_data.note: OR of 95 makes her the lowest-rated runner in the field but J J Slevin is a high-class booking and she has placed twice on Good ground in her last two starts; from a prominent position she could outrun her odds if the race is run to suit.

runners_data.name: Tanga Mugi
runners_data.note: Wore headgear previously and the hood is retained; finished seventh on Good ground over 18f on her only comparable start, and Cian Collins has had no winners in 14 days, limiting trainer confidence.

runners_data.name: That's It Girl
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's unexposed four-year-old has no recent form on record and unknown going suitability; Cromwell's 7-from-30 14-day strike rate is strong but there is simply no evidence base to assess this runner's chance meaningfully.

races.paceDynamic: Loughdoo is the sole confirmed front-runner and will set a sustainable, uncontested pace on Good to Firm ground at Down Royal, with no rival likely to seriously contest her lead through the early stages of this 2m1½f mares' maiden. Cosmic Front and Churchfield Annie will press forward into prominent positions just behind, creating a small group at the head of affairs but without the pressure that would fragment the tempo. Jo's Secret, Saoirses Choice, and Tanga Mugi are the genuine hold-up types who will settle further back, while Howaya Codge and Clanokre Lass — both natural closers — have been redistributed into midfield on the map because the rear is already crowded with hold-up horses who cannot all get their preferred position. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours prominent-racing types who can travel just behind Loughdoo, conserve energy over the first circuit, and quicken from two out — the pace is unlikely to be fierce enough to set up a late, sweeping finish for true closers.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Loughdoo controls a steady gallop and the prominent runners travelling just behind hit the front approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Cosmic Front and Churchfield Annie are well-positioned to exploit a controlled pace, travelling comfortably before delivering their challenge from two out without having burned energy fighting for position; Good to Firm ground rewards this handy, economical style over 2m1½f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Loughdoo's pace proves genuinely sustainable and the chasing pack fails to close the gap between the last two flights.
scenarios.body: With no rival applying real pressure up front, Harry Sexton's mount could dictate terms throughout and have enough in reserve to fend off challengers at the death, though her tendency to fade in the finish is a noted concern that limits confidence.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Hold-Up Winner
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly quickens mid-race and burns off the prominent runners, leaving a gap for a closer to swoop.
scenarios.body: Jo's Secret has the most credible hold-up form among the genuine rear-of-field types, showing two placed efforts on similar Good ground, and could benefit if the race is run at an honest enough clip; Tanga Mugi is lightly raced but showed pace on Good ground and could land a late blow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Howaya Codge or Clanokre Lass overcome their compromised starting positions to produce a finish from further back than ideal.
scenarios.body: Both horses are racing out of their natural hold-up role having been shuffled into midfield by the congestion at the rear, meaning they must produce their finish from a position that is not their optimum; the Style Fit discount applies and this scenario is the least likely of the four.

watchPoints.text: Cosmic Front is 203 days off the track with Brian Hayes booked for Willie Mullins — watch for market support at the off as a signal the stable is confident she's ready to go.

Loughdoo has a confirmed tendency to fade in the finish and is ridden by a 7lb claimer; if she sets only a modest pace she could be overhauled after the last even having controlled the race throughout.

Howaya Codge and Clanokre Lass are both natural hold-up types who cannot access their preferred position at the rear of this field — watch for either rider adapting their tactics early or being caught in no-man's land through the middle stages.

Messonghi is effectively a first-time-out runner for all practical purposes having only fallen previously — Rothwell's yard is in form and any strong market move on an unknown quantity here would be significant.

Rare Times carries the lowest OR in the race by a considerable margin but J J Slevin's booking for Ms Margaret Mullins elevates her interest — if she travels prominently and jumps fluently, the class jockey could make the rating gap look smaller than it is.

races.name: Golden Cow Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Lips Freedom
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who showed ability winning at this course over similar ground (1/17f/GOO) but has a documented tendency to fade in the finish — a clean jumping round will be essential, and a slow pace could see her outpaced for home; Andrew Kinirons has been quiet lately (0/2 T14).|
runners_data.comment: Lips Freedom has two wins in his last five starts and has experience over today's trip, with 27 days since his last run suggesting he returns fresh; the main risk is that he was unplaced last time out, so he must bounce back to his best.

runners_data.name: Bannow Blaze
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a modest recent record (2nd/URF/PU/F) and unplaced form over today's distance at this course on good, though similar-going history shows one win and two places from 10 runs at this type of track — needs a clean passage from the rear.|
runners_data.comment: Bannow Blaze finished second five starts back but has endured a torrid run since, pulling up, falling and unseating in his last three outings; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating just edges him to the top, though market confidence may hinge on whether that turbulent recent spell is behind him.

runners_data.name: Bruant
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who flags in the finish, yet has a genuine recent win over 2m3f on good ground and ran creditably second last time; at 5yo for a quiet-of-late trainer (0/6 T14), the fatigue risk at the end of a race on fast ground is real given the fade flag.|
runners_data.comment: Bruant won three starts back and returned to form with a second last time out, showing he retains plenty of ability off a mark of 110; he has run over today's trip before, but the 166 lb burden is the one factor that could blunt his challenge.

runners_data.name: Hopeful Hero
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner by style but tagged with a style-fit caveat (0.93) suggesting this Prominent position may itself be slightly out of character — he nevertheless is the only confirmed pace-setter and Jack Kennedy-level-calibre booking is absent here, with an amateur claiming 5lbs; course and going form is solid (10/12 sim-going).|
runners_data.comment: Hopeful Hero showed plenty two starts back with a win, but was unplaced on his most recent outing and faces a stiff task under 165 lb; he has run over today's trip and returns after 32 days off, leaving connections hopeful of a bounce-back.

runners_data.name: Only For Our Man
runners_data.note: Hold-up type that runs consistently at the top of the market in staying handicaps, with four second-place finishes in his last five and a win over 2m2f on good — the step back in trip from his recent outings could slightly blunt his staying profile but his consistency is striking.|
runners_data.comment: Consistent, with a win among his last five, Only For Our Man has finished second twice and third last time out in lively recent form, though 43 days off the track is a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and carries a hefty 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Has the best recent strike-rate in the field on similar ground (3W from 13 on good), winning most recently over 2m at a short turnaround (14 days) — a hold-up horse by style who has genuine tactical flexibility and is closely matched at OR 107 with the prominent types likely to lead.|
runners_data.comment: Small Bucks won last time out and has run over today's trip, but her patchy recent record — two wins alongside two unplaced efforts in her last six starts — and a ranking of 11th in this field suggest she faces a stiff ask under 163 lb.

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Gordon Elliott with Jack Kennedy in the saddle — the most significant jockey/trainer combination in the field and the horse most likely to sit on the girth of Hopeful Hero and apply pressure; has placed consistently on good ground over 2m but yet to win at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Dairy Force shaped well enough last time when third, and was second three starts back and fourth starts back, yet winless in recent starts and burdened by 160 lb alongside a trainer operating at just 3% over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Kazakh d'Arthel
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose natural style has him running from much further back than the map shows — the field's density of rear-runners means he may find a cleaner spot mid-division than expected; Gavin Cromwell in flying form (7/30 T14) is the key angle, and the trip and going are fine, though a wide draw could complicate matters.|
runners_data.comment: Kazakh d'Arthel won in his last five starts but has since posted a fourth, a fall, and two disappointing efforts, leaving his current form in question; he has run over today's trip and returns after 43 days off carrying 160 lb.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Holds a hurdling win on good ground over the same sort of trip and has run prominently at times (hg:p suggests hood) — though genuinely a hold-up type, his headgear and natural variation in running style mean he could race more forwardly than some other redistributed horses; the claiming jockey booking is a small negative.|
runners_data.comment: Mo Ghille Mar won four starts back but has since posted a pair of sevenths and a fourth, leaving her form looking patchy; she has run over today's trip and comes here 26 days fresh, though 160 lb is a significant burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: Certamen
runners_data.note: Has been consistently placed nowhere in recent form (P, 0, 6, 6, 5, 6) on good-to-firm equivalents with zero wins or places from eight runs at similar going — a red flag on today's conditions; the combination of poor form, no sim-going win, and a low OR makes this one to oppose.|
runners_data.comment: Certamen arrives on the back of a pull-up last time and is winless in his last four starts, which makes him hard to trust, though 25 days in between runs suggests he returns reasonably fresh and he is not without ability on a rating of 105.

runners_data.name: Golden Wings
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with limited good-ground form (2 runs, no wins or places) and a run of modest finishes, mapped to midfield only due to overcrowding at the rear — style fit is discounted (0.90) and the sim-going record does not inspire confidence on this surface today.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled-up and two deep finishes among recent efforts, Golden Wings faces a stiff ask off 158 lb for a trainer firing at just 3% lately; experience over today's trip is the one crumb of comfort.

runners_data.name: Viceregent
runners_data.note: Returns from a 310-day absence in a 16-runner handicap for a trainer with no recent winners — the absence alone is a major concern, and this horse's form best came on softer ground over shorter trips; the redistribution means he cannot even settle in his natural spot.|
runners_data.comment: Rated 114 and ranked second of 16, Viceregent shaped with plenty of promise when fourth and fifth in recent starts, and that form makes him a serious threat on a return from 310 days off — though his pulled-up latest effort and winless run in his last five starts are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Home By The Sea
runners_data.note: Rated for a late run but has faded in the finish in recent starts and is consistently beaten well back in field (6th, 16th, 15th, 4th, 12th) — the redistribution forces a mid-division placement that is not natural, and the fade flag on fast ground makes this a horse to be sceptical of.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom two on our figures, Home By The Sea faces a stiff ask at 154 lb, though a return to action after just 18 days at least suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Kilt
runners_data.note: Has a win and multiple places at this sort of trip on good ground (1W2P from 13) and is consistent — though a hold-up type pushed into map midfield, his jockey Simon Torrens is in form at this meeting and the trainer (3/13 T14) is live; the style compromise is real but manageable for a consistent horse.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked well below the principals on our figures, Kilt has managed just one win in his last five starts, with three fourth-or-worse efforts since, and carrying 154 lb does him no favours; he has run over today's trip before, and 25 days between runs leaves him reasonably fresh.

runners_data.name: Whispering Willow
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on good ground and has placed twice in staying handicaps at this level — a hold-up horse in the redistribution pack, but Gavin Cromwell's second string here after Kazakh d'Arthel; genuine staying form (3/19f/GOO, 3/20f/GOO) gives hope if the pace quickens and she can deliver a sustained run.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 14 of 16 on our figures, Whispering Willow is hard to fancy despite a win and two thirds in recent starts; she has run over today's trip and returns after 35 days, but her last two outings — unplaced and sixth — make a turnaround difficult to argue for.

runners_data.name: Your Call
runners_data.note: The youngest and lightest-weighted runner in the field (4yo, 151lbs) returning from 45 days off, with unimpressive recent form (8th, 10th, 9th) and a claiming 7lb apprentice; the hold-up style is natural but the redistribution and weak form make this hard to back.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of this field on our figures, Your Call faces a stiff ask off 151 lb; he has run over today's trip and returns after 45 days, but an eighth last time out offers little encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Hopeful Hero is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 16-runner field and, critically, faces no genuine challenger for the lead — this sets up a controlled, sustainable gallop on good-to-firm ground at Down Royal rather than a pressured, frantic early pace. With Dairy Force the only other horse mapped as prominent and capable of tracking closely, Hopeful Hero can dictate terms from the front without burning excessive energy, meaning the race will likely be run at an honest but not searingly fast pace, with the field strung out behind from an early stage. The absence of true pace pressure plays directly into the hands of hold-up horses who can travel through the race, but the controlled tempo also means prominent trackers sitting just off the pace may get first crack at the winner when the front-runner comes back to them in the closing stages — this shape best suits a well-positioned close tracker with a strong finish or a high-class hold-up horse with serious late acceleration. Several runners tagged REDISTRIBUTED — including Kazakh d'Arthel, Mo Ghille Mar, Golden Wings, Viceregent, Home By The Sea, Kilt, Whispering Willow, and Your Call — are genuine hold-up types pushed into map midfield positions because the field carries more rear-runners than can all sit where they want; of these, Kazakh d'Arthel and Mo Ghille Mar are most likely to actually secure a workable position closer to the pace than their tags suggest.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hopeful Hero Controls, Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Hopeful Hero sets a steady, uncontested pace and a close-order tracker lands a telling blow turning in.
scenarios.body: Hopeful Hero dictates a comfortable gallop from the front, with Dairy Force or a prominent-type sitting within two lengths and hitting the front entering the straight before hold-up horses can get organised; on good-to-firm ground at this trip the race could set up beautifully for a horse who has travelled through it under a calm pace and has petrol left at the business end.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Soft Pace Collapses In Straight
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled tempo causes a bunching effect and the race becomes a sprint from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: A modest early gallop leaves multiple horses in contention rounding the home turn, producing a messy, competitive finish where class and OR rather than pace placement determine the outcome; horses with high RPR and clean jumping — regardless of style — benefit most from this scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: True Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace picks up mid-race and the hold-up horses who are genuinely running from the rear get a proper test to finish into.
scenarios.body: A stronger-than-expected tempo through the body of the race, possibly triggered by Dairy Force pressing Hopeful Hero, strings the field out and the late-runners who can travel wide and produce sustained finishes get first run on tired rivals; discount slightly because most of the redistibuted hold-up types in this field face a style compromise and may not secure the position needed to deliver a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hopeful Hero Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If the lone front-runner is never pressured and the gap to the chasing pack grows through the final mile.
scenarios.body: Hopeful Hero, exploiting a complete lack of pace pressure, controls every yard of the contest and simply has more left in the tank than hold-up horses making up ground from deep; though tagged with a style-fit caveat, the absence of a rival willing or able to press him makes this a genuine possibility on fast ground.

watchPoints.text: Dairy Force and Hopeful Hero — if Jack Kennedy moves Dairy Force to track the front-runner early, this is no longer an uncontested lead scenario and the entire race shape changes from controlled to pressured.

Multiple redistributed hold-up horses (Kazakh d'Arthel, Mo Ghille Mar, Kilt, Whispering Willow) will all be jostling for a workable position from the rear — watch for traffic problems and potential interference at the hurdles as the pace steadies and the field bunches.

Hopeful Hero carries a STYLE_FIT caveat of 0.93 — if he fails to stride on naturally in front and gets swamped by Dairy Force or another, the race shape collapses entirely and front-running scenario probabilities drop sharply.

Small Bucks arrives on a short 14-day turnaround having won his last start — watch the market move here as any significant support at that interval signals trainer confidence the horse has trained on well enough for a quick reappearance.

The going is officially Good To Firm at Down Royal for all seven races today — no sign of any deterioration expected, so horses with solid fast-ground form profiles (Small Bucks, Hopeful Hero, Only For Our Man) retain their advantage throughout the afternoon.

races.name: Pepsico (Walkers Snacks) Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Hidden Empire
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and showed only a modest effort on soft over 2m at latest start, with a noted tendency to fade in the finish that is a real concern stepping up to 2m4f on faster ground; unknown quantity whose style is unclassified.|

runners_data.name: Santa Domingo

runners_data.name: Seamy Appletart

runners_data.name: Teddy Jones

runners_data.name: Wackestone

runners_data.name: Wee Fallon

runners_data.name: Lisnadill
runners_data.note: McBratney's charge carries the plum conditions weight of 146lbs and has shown two placed efforts from 10 sim-going runs — genuinely a hold-up horse by profile, but the field's volume of rear-dwellers means it is likely to race closer to midfield than ideal, a redistribution that tempers its prospects materially; Sexton rides.|

runners_data.name: Oops A Daisy
runners_data.note: Hanlon's runner has three consecutive Good-ground runs all resulting in mid-to-rear finishes without threatening, and the fade flag compounds the concern; like Lisnadill it is a true hold-up type who will struggle to access its natural position at the rear, making the out-of-role mapping a genuine disadvantage rather than a minor inconvenience.|

races.paceDynamic: Santa Domingo is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into an uncontested, sustainable rhythm on Good to Firm ground over 2m4f at Down Royal. With Lisnadill and Oops A Daisy both true hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural rear positions in this shape, they have been mapped to midfield — meaning the race is effectively split between Santa Domingo up front and a cluster of hold-up/midfield horses tracking behind. This controlled, single-paced scenario over an extended trip strongly favours a prominent racer who can travel within striking distance of Santa Domingo without expending unnecessary energy, then produce a clean jump at the last and quicken. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than can realistically settle at the rear, with Lisnadill and Oops A Daisy the horses most likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than they would prefer, which further consolidates the advantage for prominent-to-midfield runners who travel naturally in that zone — making Wackestone a natural beneficiary of the shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Santa Domingo dictates an honest but uncontested gallop and a prominent tracker attacks from the second-last.
scenarios.body: Santa Domingo sets a manageable tempo that rewards horses travelling smoothly just off the pace, with the Good to Firm surface ensuring a premium on fluent jumping and stamina rather than a late burst; prominent runners who save energy through the race will be best placed turning in.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds, Front Runner Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Santa Domingo's uncontested lead proves too comfortable and no challenger has the gears to close the gap from the second-last.
scenarios.body: On Good to Firm ground with no pressure applied, Santa Domingo could find a second wind in the straight having lobbed round in front and jumped cleanly; this rewards the horse with the best hurdle technique and fresh legs after a long layoff, and Wackestone cannot quicken enough to reel in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that hold-up horses can close ground rapidly in the final two flights despite their compromised starting positions.
scenarios.body: Lisnadill or Oops A Daisy would need to find a better closing run than their recent form suggests and overcome the reality that they are unlikely to get true hold-up berths; the style-fit discounts here are material — both are tagged as racing out of role — making this the least natural outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Faders Collide, Surprise Result
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners including Santa Domingo fade dramatically in the final half-mile and a midfield horse with fresh legs gets first run.
scenarios.body: Hidden Empire and Teddy Jones are both lightly raced and flagged as faders, so they would need to reverse that tendency; if the pace somehow collapses into a scramble at the final flights, one of the unknown quantities could profit, but the evidence for this shape is thin given the likely controlled tempo.

watchPoints.text: Santa Domingo's 335-day layoff is the single biggest variable in this race — if fitness is lacking, the seemingly comfortable lead could evaporate dramatically from the third-last, fundamentally changing who benefits from the collapse.

Wackestone is using a 7lb claimer (Joshua Halford) in what could be a pace-dependent scenario — a jumping error or positional misjudgement in the early stages could cost the horse the prominent berth it needs.

Lisnadill and Oops A Daisy are both genuine hold-up horses forced toward midfield by the density of rear-dwellers in this field — watch whether either can find clear daylight from two out, because if they do, the late-run scenario becomes live.

Good to Firm conditions (confirmed for this race in the going report) place a premium on clean hurdle jumping — horses with any jumping concerns, particularly over 2m4f, face a compounding stamina and technical test that could expose weaknesses not visible on softer surfaces.

Hidden Empire and Teddy Jones are both lightly raced with unclassified styles and fade flags — if either shows a markedly different profile to their single hurdle run, the race shape could be redrawn, but current evidence does not support backing either to lead the way home.

races.name: Denny Hurdle

runners_data.comment: Gangster Granny arrives in good heart with wins last time out and two starts back, but she is ranked bottom of this field on our figures and carries 153 lb, making it hard to fancy her against stronger-rated rivals despite that recent winning thread.

races.paceDynamic: Rocky's Diamond and The Friday Man are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the outset over this testing 3m trip on Good to Firm ground at Down Royal, creating a genuinely contested gallop rather than a soft-pedalled lead. With Rocky's Diamond carrying higher class (OR=147) and a more experienced jockey pairing in this role, he is the likeliest to control the pace, though The Friday Man will push him throughout the early and middle stages. That honest, pressured gallop over 3m on a quick surface will stretch the field and place a premium on jumping fluency and stamina, favouring horses who can travel prominently without over-committing, or sit just off the pace and absorb the tempo before asserting late. Note that this field carries more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Ambitious Fellow and Gangster Granny are genuine closers by nature but have been redistributed to midfield given the congestion; Reverend Hubert, Thecompanysergeant, and Samui are the true hold-up contingent most likely to secure their natural positions, and of those, Reverend Hubert and Samui have the class and track profiles to exploit a honest gallop from the rear. The race shape strongly favours prominent horses with stamina reserves and quality hold-up horses who can deliver a sustained late challenge — flat-track speed specialists or horses requiring a falsely-run race are at a structural disadvantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Honest Gallop, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond and The Friday Man set a genuine contested pace that stretches the field throughout, burning off lesser stayers in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners run each other honest and the race becomes a true stamina test over the final mile, rewarding horses who conserve energy by travelling fluidly just behind the pace or absorbing the gallop from further back with class. Loch Cuan, tracking prominently with strong Good-ground form, and Reverend Hubert, a proven 3m performer with exceptional Good-going figures, are best placed to capitalise.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Diamond shakes off The Friday Man early, controls tempo at his own pace, and jumps fluently throughout to dictate on his terms.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Diamond, the highest-rated runner in the field at OR=147, is capable of setting a controlled gallop that is fast enough to string the field out but measured enough to preserve his own stamina reserves over 3m. If The Friday Man fails to maintain contact after a flat-out 384-day absence, Rocky's Diamond could dictate unchallenged and prove too strong for hold-up horses giving him too much rope.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is brutally contested and both front-runners tie up in the final half-mile, leaving a vacuum for true closers to sweep through.
scenarios.body: A punishing early gallop between Rocky's Diamond and The Friday Man depletes both before the final turn, creating an opportunity for confirmed hold-up horses tracking from further back to deliver fresh finishing runs. Reverend Hubert and Samui, both genuine hold-up operators with class and Good-ground form, are the natural beneficiaries if the front-runners genuinely run each other into the ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is moderate rather than genuinely contested and the race compresses into a tactical affair with a late sprint for home.
scenarios.body: A surprisingly muted gallop would see the field bunch together, turning the race into a jumping-and-quickening contest rather than a stamina test, slightly boosting prominently-tracked horses with better finishing speed. Clay Pigeons, with strong form on Good ground for Mullins, and Thecompanysergeant, proven at this trip and track conditions, hold each-way claims if the anticipated pace never truly materialises.

watchPoints.text: Rocky's Diamond and The Friday Man — if both dig in early and refuse to yield, the pace could be genuinely fierce over 3m on Good to Firm, dramatically compressing finishing positions and making jumping errors in the final mile decisive.

The Friday Man's 384-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the field — if he sets a true pace before dying, the race shape is entirely altered; if he fades after a mile, Rocky's Diamond leads unchallenged and the entire dynamic changes.

Samui's quick turnaround (7 days since last run) combined with hood and tongue-strap headgear warrants monitoring at the start and over early hurdles — Kennedy will need to find a clean rhythm from the outset to keep him in contention.

Gangster Granny and Ambitious Fellow — both genuine hold-up horses pushed into a midfield position by field congestion; if either secures an unimpeded run up the straight they could outrun their map position, but punters should not assume they will get clear daylight.

Loch Cuan's step up to 3m is uncharted territory — watch whether James Smith (5lb claim) settles him prominently in the early stages without over-committing, as the trip question will only be answered in the final half-mile.

races.paceDynamic: Fire Coral is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of 22, and on Good to Firm ground over 3m at Down Royal will be allowed to bowl along unchallenged, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop that is unlikely to stretch the field early. With just three horses carrying a Prominent tag — Jonny Carrol, Charlie's Dilemma, and Georgia Celena — the pace picture is remarkably thin for such a large field, meaning Fire Coral will almost certainly dictate on his own terms with minimal pressure through the early and middle stages. The bulk of the field is genuine hold-up or midfield types, but so many of them have been redistributed off the back that the map is congested in the middle section; Brandt, Sneddy Eddie, Grace Faraday, Moonshine Girl, Clever Court, Whatyouwant, Gypsy Poet, Sekifi, Technology, My Policy and Le Grand Vert are true hold-up horses who simply cannot all get their natural position in a field this size, and those most likely to actually secure space near the rear are the better-credentialled hold-up performers such as Knocknagoran Lady, Bayonetta, and Journey So Far who have the tactical nous and class to find clean air. A lone front-runner setting a measured, uncontested gallop over 3m on quick ground strongly favours horses who can track or sit just off the pace in the prominent-to-midfield bracket and produce a sustained gallop into the straight, rather than deep closers who will need a collapsing pace to overhaul Fire Coral — the pace simply may not collapse enough.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Fire Coral Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Fire Coral bowls along in front and the prominent trackers fail to land a serious challenge turning in.
scenarios.body: Fire Coral sets a measured, controlled pace and the field strings out on the Good to Firm surface, meaning he conserves enough energy to repel all comers up the straight; horses who can track closely in the prominent-to-midfield bracket and quicken on this ground are best placed to pounce if he weakens.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent or close-tracking horses sits a length or two off Fire Coral and overpowers him in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: On Good to Firm ground over 3m the prominent position is golden when the pace is honest but not fierce, allowing a horse like Knocknagoran Lady or Georgia Celena to travel comfortably and produce a strong staying finish without burning energy early; this is the shape that most suits horses with a proven good-ground record and the class to accelerate at the end of a long-distance jumps race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Hold-Up Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If Fire Coral sets a stronger gallop than expected and the field is sufficiently strung out that a well-placed midfield horse can pick off tiring rivals.
scenarios.body: Bayonetta and Knocknagoran Lady, both consistent on this ground and genuinely effective over staying trips, are best positioned to arrive late if the pace causes enough attrition; however, the congested midfield and the sustainable nature of Fire Coral's likely gallop reduce the chance that the lead will be caught cold.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Up Arrives Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so modest that hold-up horses at the rear find themselves with too much ground to make up in the straight.
scenarios.body: With the majority of the field redistributed away from their natural rear position and Fire Coral setting only a gentle pace, deep closers will find insufficient gaps and a collapsing tempo — this shape suits almost nobody in the field and the redistributed hold-up horses are the most exposed; Brandt and Le Grand Vert have the staying profile to at least finish on but are unlikely to get competitive.

watchPoints.text: Fire Coral holds all the pace cards — watch whether the prominent horses Jonny Carrol, Georgia Celena, or Charlie's Dilemma apply any pressure early; if they don't, Fire Coral could prove very hard to peg back at the top of the straight.

Knocknagoran Lady's jockey Conor Stone-Walsh must navigate a 22-runner field from a hold-up position — any traffic trouble turning for home could cost her the race if this scenario unfolds as a close-run thing.

Jack Kennedy on Sneddy Eddie is the headline jockey booking, but Sneddy Eddie is a redistributed hold-up horse who may not get his natural ground — watch for Kennedy to try to push forward earlier than the horse's usual style would suggest.

Journey So Far carries a finishing fade flag for Keith Donoghue — if this horse hits the front prematurely or is drawn into a battle too early, the fade profile makes him unreliable late over this 3m trip on good ground.

My Policy has no jockey listed at entry time — monitor market and declaration confirmation, as a late booking could signal either stable confidence or a tactical change that affects the race's hold-up cluster dynamic.

runners_data.name: Clovelly Charm
runners_data.comment: Clovelly Charm won last time out and, with just two starts to her name, remains unexposed and open to plenty of improvement; the 47-day absence is the main query under a big 165 lb burden.

runners_data.name: Missouri Snow
runners_data.comment: Missouri Snow arrives in red-hot form, winning her last two starts in succession, and 22 days between runs suggests she comes here fresh and ready; the chief concern is whether 165 lb at the top of the weights will blunt her momentum.

runners_data.name: Hilly Filly
runners_data.comment: Hilly Filly won on her sole recent start and remains unexposed, but 49 days off the track and a trainer without a winner in the last 14 days are factors to weigh against her at 162 lb.

runners_data.name: Bredas Pearl
runners_data.comment: Bredas Pearl arrives here in fine fettle after consecutive placed efforts, third two starts back and second last time out, and has run over today's trip before. Winless in her last three, she nonetheless profiles as the one to beat on her rating heading a field of 12.

runners_data.name: Bresil Belle
runners_data.comment: Bresil Belle makes her debut carrying 158 lb, completely unexposed and with everything still to prove — a mare to watch closely as she finds her feet in the race environment.

runners_data.name: Cave Daisy
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Cave Daisy steps into the unknown carrying 158 lb, but her unraced profile leaves plenty to work with and she could be anything as connections find out what they have.

runners_data.name: Maxdale Prinxess
runners_data.comment: Unexposed on debut, Maxdale Prinxess carries 158 lb into the unknown but remains open to any amount of improvement as connections find out what she is capable of at this first opportunity.

runners_data.name: Poet's Creek
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to any amount of improvement on debut, Poet's Creek is yet to score under rules and arrives carrying 158 lb, leaving the imagination free to fill in the gaps.

runners_data.name: Anna Quaintance
runners_data.comment: Anna Quaintance has run over today's trip and, rated 74 among these rivals, she represents a live threat back over a proven distance — the concern is that her fifth last time out leaves her yet to score in recent starts and she will need to find improvement.

runners_data.name: Hutton Star
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Hutton Star steps onto the track carrying 155 lb with everything still to prove but with all questions still to be answered by the racecourse.

runners_data.name: Junction Road
runners_data.comment: Unraced and open to plenty of improvement, Junction Road steps into the unknown on debut carrying 155 lb, with her unexposed profile leaving plenty to work with as connections find out what she is capable of.

runners_data.name: Molly Des Bruyeres
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Molly Des Bruyeres is yet to score under rules and arrives as an unknown quantity, but carrying 155 lb is the key physical challenge she faces first time out.
